Button

Anatomy

Pay with card
  1. 1.dr-btnThe control. min-height 44, never a fixed height, so a scrolling column cannot shrink it below the 44pt target. Radius 12, padding 0 16.
  2. 2.dr-icAn optional leading glyph, 20px, 8px before the label, drawn in the label's ink. Pay with card in the order-review pay drawer.
  3. 3.dr-btn--primaryThe fill. Signal Green behind a charcoal label, 9.46:1, with the one shadow rung a resting control may carry.

When to use

A button is a verb the user commits to. The system spends one green control per screen. Every action bar holds one primary at most; account-photo and operator-account-photo gave up their second one at rev 292. The primary button carries the screen's main job and covers 81–100% of that screen's green, while everything else that can be tapped is warm grey. In the action bar every button is filled and stacks one per row at full width, primary first, so no label wraps at 320pt. Text-only rungs (tertiary, text) live in navigation bars and inside cards, never on the bottom edge.

Two rungs in DESIGN.md are not in the live system. Outline (pill, slate edge) and destructive text are declared in the ui/kit.css archive, but no screen draws them, so they were never ported into components/. The first screen that needs one brings it in, and this page follows.

The label is the outcome, not the mechanism: Pay ₴180, Rate this order, Report an issue. One word stands for one concept: Contact support to reach a person, Try again to recover, Withdraw for money out. No exclamation marks and no successfully. A price is stated in the label before the tap, the way P3 of the voice asks.

Sources: DESIGN.md § Buttons · § Named rules (One Accent, Built Not Dimmed) · voice.md P1, P3 · microcopy.md § Inconsistency catalogue · inventory.md § 1.2

Rule and anti-rule

Do

Rate this order Report an issue

The action bar of inspection-report: one primary for the screen's job and a secondary for the way out, both full width, one per row. The primary is on top in every action bar (rev 290).

Don’t

Two green buttons split across one row. A second primary spends the screen's only accent twice, and a split row is where labels wrap. Make the second action a secondary on its own row. To pick between routes rather than commit to one, use a choice card.
